course.title: AI-Powered DevOps Automation with n8n
course.subtitle: Self-host n8n and Mattermost, automate deployments, Kubernetes alerts, incidents and reports, then add AI summaries safely: redacted logs, labelled drafts and a human who decides.
course.description:
Your systems produce events all day: a deployment fails at 3 a.m., a pod keeps crashing, a report is due. In this course you automate the work around those events with **n8n**, deliver the result where your team already talks (**Mattermost**), and add **AI** where it genuinely helps: a model that reads the log and drafts a summary, while a person stays in charge.

## What you'll build
- A self-hosted **n8n + Mattermost** stack with Docker Compose, on your computer or on an **AWS EC2 VM created with Terraform** and reached through an SSH tunnel.
- **Deployment notifications** from a CI pipeline (with a GitHub Actions example): green or red in the team channel, protected by a secret token.
- Workflows that **fail safely**: retries, a fallback path, an error workflow that alerts the team, and node-by-node debugging.
- **Kubernetes alerts** for crash loops, stuck rollouts and unschedulable pods, one message per problem, plus a daily namespace health report.
- **Incident management**: repeated alerts become one incident with a severity, escalation when nobody acknowledges, and a resolved message.
- **Scheduled reports** that collect deployments, failures and service status every morning.
- **AI-assisted workflows** with OpenAI: a summary of a failed deployment (what failed, the likely cause, what to check), an error explainer, an incident summary and an AI-written morning report. Secrets, IP addresses and e-mails are redacted before anything is sent, logs are treated as untrusted text (prompt injection), every answer is labelled as a draft with its token cost, and a human reviews it. The AI never changes anything.

## Who this course is for
DevOps engineers, SREs and developers who are comfortable with a terminal and Docker and want to automate the notifications, alerts and reports around their systems, and to use AI in those workflows responsibly.

## Tools and technologies
n8n, Mattermost, Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, Redis (queue mode), Kubernetes (minikube and kubectl), Alertmanager-style alerts, GitHub Actions (example pipeline), webhooks and HMAC signatures, cron schedules, OpenAI (n8n's AI node; Amazon Bedrock and Azure AI Foundry are explained as alternatives), Terraform and AWS EC2.

## How the course is organised
Four sections, from your first workflow to production:
1. **Getting started**: what n8n and Mattermost do, deploy both, channels and incoming webhooks, your first workflows, and the same lab on a cloud VM.
2. **Core concepts and your first real automations**: n8n vocabulary, deployment notifications, errors, retries and debugging.
3. **DevOps automations in practice**: automation and ChatOps vocabulary, Kubernetes alerts, incident management and scheduled reports.
4. **Advanced patterns and production**: sub-workflows, signed webhooks, idempotency, rate limits, pagination and loop guards; n8n in production (Postgres, queue mode with workers, the encryption key, backups, upgrades and rollback); and AI-assisted workflows, safely.

Every idea starts with an everyday example, then you see it running live. Each hands-on lesson comes with its slides (PDF) and a lab (ZIP) with the Compose files, scripts and workflows from the video, and most lessons end with a short quiz with the answers explained.

## Prerequisites
- Comfortable with a terminal and basic Docker commands.
- Docker with the Compose plugin, or a cloud VM where you can install it (the lab needs about 4 GB of free memory).
- For the Kubernetes lesson: minikube and kubectl (the lab explains both), or your own EKS or AKS cluster.
- For the AI lesson: your own OpenAI API key, with a monthly budget limit set.
- For the cloud VM lesson (optional): an AWS account with a budget alarm, the AWS CLI and Terraform 1.5 or newer. A one-hour lab costs a few cents; you delete everything with terraform destroy.
objectives: Deploy n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose, locally or on an AWS EC2 VM created with Terraform, and keep their data
Create Mattermost channels and incoming webhooks, and keep webhook URLs and secrets out of your workflows
Build n8n workflows with triggers, nodes, expressions and executions, and publish them to run on their own
Send green and red deployment notifications from a CI pipeline through a token-protected webhook
Make workflows fail safely with retries, fallback paths, error workflows and step-by-step debugging
Watch a Kubernetes namespace and post one clear alert per problem, without duplicate floods
Turn alerts into incidents with severity, escalation, acknowledgement and resolution
Schedule reports that collect deployments, failures and service status every morning
Apply sub-workflows, signed webhooks, idempotency, rate limits, pagination and loop guards
Run n8n in production with Postgres, queue mode, the encryption key, backups, upgrades and rollback
Add AI summaries of failed deployments, errors and incidents with OpenAI: redacted input, labelled drafts, human review
Defend AI workflows against secret leaks and prompt injection, and keep an eye on token costs

lessons.title: What n8n and Mattermost do for a DevOps team
lessons.summary: Triggers, workflows, channels and incoming webhooks explained with one everyday example, and why DevOps teams self-host n8n and Mattermost together.

lessons.title: Deploy n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose
lessons.summary: Read the Compose file block by block, start n8n, Mattermost and a demo site, fix a real port conflict, log in to both apps and prove your data survives new containers.

lessons.title: Set up Mattermost for automation: channels and incoming webhooks
lessons.summary: Tour Mattermost, create an alerts channel and its incoming webhook, keep the webhook URL in .env, and prove that n8n can post to it from inside Docker.

lessons.title: Tour n8n and build your first workflows
lessons.summary: Every n8n menu and settings page, then two workflows that post real messages to Mattermost: run them by hand, publish them, fix a real error and read every run in Executions.

lessons.title: Run the automation lab on a cloud VM with Terraform
lessons.summary: Create an AWS EC2 VM with Terraform, start the same n8n and Mattermost lab on it and reach it through an SSH tunnel. Only SSH from your IP is open; then terraform destroy and check that nothing is left.

sections.title: Core concepts and your first real automations

lessons.title: n8n vocabulary: workflows, triggers, nodes, items and executions
lessons.summary: Workflow, trigger, node, item, expression, execution and publish, one word at a time: an everyday example, an animation, then the real n8n screen.

lessons.title: Deployment notifications from your CI pipeline
lessons.summary: A CI pipeline calls an n8n webhook after each deployment and the team sees a green or red message in Mattermost, protected by a token so forged calls get a 401.

lessons.title: Errors, retries and debugging
lessons.summary: Retries, a fallback path, an error workflow that alerts the team, and debugging a failed execution node by node with pinned mock data, against an API that fails on purpose.

lessons.title: Automation and ChatOps vocabulary
lessons.summary: Webhook or polling, cron, sub-workflows, idempotency, rate limits, queue mode and slash commands, explained with one café example, then where you meet each in n8n and Mattermost.

lessons.title: Kubernetes alerts in Mattermost
lessons.summary: n8n checks a namespace every 30 seconds and posts one clear alert for crash loops, stuck rollouts and unschedulable pods, without duplicates, plus a daily namespace health report.

lessons.title: Incident management: severity, escalation and resolution
lessons.summary: Turn repeated alerts into one incident with a severity, escalate when nobody acknowledges, and close the loop with a resolved message, on a real outage.

lessons.title: Scheduled reports for your team
lessons.summary: Schedule Trigger workflows that collect deployments, failures and service status, write a short report and post it to Mattermost every morning.

lessons.title: Advanced workflow design
lessons.summary: Sub-workflows, signed webhooks, idempotency, rate limits and batches, pagination, loop guards, workflows in git and where the logs are, each one run for real.

lessons.title: Running n8n in production
lessons.summary: Postgres, queue mode with workers, the encryption key, backups and restores, pinned upgrades with a rollback, and a disaster recovery drill.

lessons.title: AI-assisted workflows, safely
lessons.summary: AI summaries of failed deployments, incidents and errors: sensitive data removed first, output labelled as a draft, and a human always decides.
